claim_being_audited: That rejecting vendor Kestrel-Borderline-040 was policy-compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved control risk at the time of approval.
specific_concerns: The packet plausibly supports follow-up or escalation, but the policy requires evidence of a material unresolved risk for rejection, and materiality is asserted rather than demonstrated.
A questionnaire-to-attachment inconsistency and an undocumented quality process are, under the policy text, not by themselves proof of a reject-level control failure.
The procurement note appears conditional: it recommends follow-up before approval if storage controls remained unresolved, which is weaker than a documented recommendation to reject.
The summary says there was no logged resolution, but the auditor does not have the underlying record to confirm the absence of a formal resolution entry at decision time.

Countervailing evidence on price and prior delivery history does not defeat rejection by itself, but it raises the importance of showing why the unresolved issue was materially disqualifying rather than merely escalatory.
unsupported_claims: That the documented file, as opposed to the actor's characterization of it, establishes reject-level materiality rather than a need for follow-up or escalation.
That the unresolved storage-control issue remained open at the exact decision point with no formal logged resolution.
Any implication that the record proves a confirmed control failure rather than an unresolved diligence question.
evidence_requests: The actual contents of BPROC-040-D and BPROC-040-E showing the storage-control variance and the procurement follow-up language.
A dated approval timeline or decision log showing the issue was still unresolved when the rejection decision was made.
Any admissible document establishing why the storage-control issue was material enough to justify rejection rather than conditional approval, remediation, or escalation.
The reviewed control-binder record or equivalent showing what quality-process documentation was missing and why that gap was decision-critical.
decision_criteria: Rejecting a vendor is compliant only if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk.
Questionnaire inconsistencies and quality-process gaps can justify follow-up or escalation, but do not alone establish reject-level failure.
Conditional procurement language supporting follow-up before approval is weaker than a direct documented recommendation to reject.
The conclusion must rest on admissible logged evidence, not inferred or private review results.
